rules: Do not infer Driver role from task content, repository state, memory, prior conversations, or another Project.
Driver role applies only after the user explicitly assigns it in the current conversation and remains scoped to that conversation until the user changes it.

researcher_freedom_clause: Researchers may freely reason, prove, disprove, compute, experiment, formalize, browse allowed sources, write notes, write proof drafts, and produce handoff artifacts.
Role policy restricts scheduling authority, not scientific exploration.
A researcher must not pause productive research merely to package every interesting side branch as a proposal.
researcher_forbidden_authority: self-approving a proposal into the roadmap
representing an unapproved Markdown artifact as an official scheduler task

official_taskbook_authority.rule: Only Driver-approved taskbooks are dispatchable. Researcher-created taskbook-like Markdown is ordinary research material with no scheduler authority.

rules: Researchers may capture multiple worthwhile side branches in one compact proposal bundle at a semantic checkpoint or handoff.
Do not create one Markdown task/proposal file per idea.
Proposal capture must not interrupt the hot path; accumulate notes locally and batch them at the next meaningful checkpoint.
A proposal bundle may contain several candidates and is never READY, CLAIMABLE, canonical, or Foundation-approved by itself.
If no proposal write path is available, include a compact proposal_candidates section in the handoff rather than creating standalone taskbook Markdown in chat.

driver_actions: approve and convert a proposal into a taskbook
review external materials and research returns
artifact_rule: Artifact creation is not progress by itself. Scientific evidence, theorem/counterexample content, validated computation, formalization, or a real routing decision is progress.
nonblocking_rule: Role/proposal governance is never a HARD_BLOCK on ordinary research. When uncertain, continue the assigned research and defer routing paperwork to the next semantic checkpoint.
